title: Databases
description: SQL vs NoSQL, SQL, ORMs, keys, relationships, joins, indexes, transactions, ACID, normalization, replicas, sharding, and consistency.

lessons.title: Relational and NoSQL Databases
lessons.summary: SQL fits structured relational data; NoSQL fits flexible schemas, caching, and document workloads.
lessons.explanation: SQL fits structured relational data; NoSQL fits flexible schemas, caching, and document workloads. In interviews, explain the concept, when it applies, and the trade-off it introduces. Use concrete examples from the provided material instead of definitions alone.
examples: Orders referencing users are naturally relational.
interview_questions: When would you apply relational and nosql databases?
What failure mode appears when relational and nosql databases is misunderstood?

lessons.title: Keys, Relationships, and JOINs
lessons.summary: Primary keys identify rows; foreign keys connect tables; JOINs combine related data.

lessons.title: Indexes and Transactions
lessons.summary: Indexes speed reads at write cost; transactions keep multi-step changes consistent.
lessons.explanation: Indexes speed reads at write cost; transactions keep multi-step changes consistent. In interviews, explain the concept, when it applies, and the trade-off it introduces. Use concrete examples from the provided material instead of definitions alone.

lessons.title: Replication, Sharding, and Consistency
lessons.summary: Read replicas copy data for reads; sharding splits data; eventual consistency accepts temporary staleness.
lessons.explanation: Read replicas copy data for reads; sharding splits data; eventual consistency accepts temporary staleness. In interviews, explain the concept, when it applies, and the trade-off it introduces. Use concrete examples from the provided material instead of definitions alone.
examples: A social feed can tolerate a short delay before a new like appears.

coding_challenges.title: Databases status classifier
coding_challenges.instructions: Implement classify_status_code(code: int) -> str. Return success for 200-299, redirect for 300-399, client_error for 400-499, server_error for 500-599, and unknown otherwise.
coding_challenges.explanation: The challenge reinforces deterministic branching, status-code categories, and local test execution.
